pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all 0 and that done = 2 is rejected.
src/index.js uses the default view 'open' with WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id. 'AC-2' marks item 2 done and checks that / and /?view=open both list only the other two items.
The done view uses WHERE done = 1, and item() prefixes ✓. 'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
The all view has no WHERE clause. 'AC-4' expects all three items in id order with only the done one marked ✓.
nav() renders the current view as <strong> and the others as links. 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /.
Object.hasOwn rejects unknown values, '__proto__' and the empty string, and returns 400 with no list. 'AC-6' covers Open, closed, '' and __proto__, and checks that no <li> appears.
The code runs a COUNT query to choose between 'No items yet.' and the per-view message. 'AC-7' and the Empty table, Nothing open and Nothing done state tests cover all three messages.
traffic/routes.json is ["/","/?view=done","/?view=all"]. 'AC-8' asserts both routes are present. traffic/src/index.js appends each route to the request URL, so the query is sent.

findings.what: The PR says the checker 'now accepts' a route with a query string. The regex /^\/[^\s#]*$/ already allows '?', and I could not diff the old version because Bash was refused. If the script was not changed, the claim is inaccurate. If it was changed, I could not see how.
findings.fix: Confirm against the diff and drop or correct the claim in the PR body if the script is unchanged.

findings.what: AC-1 only checks freshly seeded rows. It does not prove that rows that existed before the migration start open, because the seed is applied after all migrations. The DEFAULT 0 clause does guarantee this.
findings.fix: Optional: apply 0001, insert a row, then apply 0002 and assert done = 0.

lenses.note: The spec has a go from the owner. The decisions are followed: the default view is open, and the view is a query parameter on a GET-only app.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented. Nothing outside the spec's scope was added: there is no write route and no remembered view.
Each acceptance item and each state has a behavioural test. The traffic test fake now records the query string, and no tests were deleted. Only the low AC-1 note above.
The README describes the views. The routes.json comment in the README stays accurate.
The view value is checked against a whitelist with hasOwn, and the SQL fragments come only from constants. The empty-table logic is correct. No dead code.
The query parameter is only whitelist-matched and never interpolated from input. Titles are still HTML-escaped. No instructions were planted in the repository content.
I could not run a browser. The page is a minimal server-rendered HTML list, and the nav markup is covered by tests.
There is no browser in the session and no UI flow was demonstrated. The nav and states are covered by HTTP-level tests.
The title and claims match the diff as far as I could read it. The one uncertain claim is the low finding on the traffic route checker.
